page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores powered by AWS Graviton processors implementing the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. With one thread per core, the system eliminates hyper-threading contention. It is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local storage, depending entirely on remote elastic block storage, and does not contain discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Network throughput is a primary capability of this configuration, offering a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate exceptional multi-threaded performance alongside high cached memory bandwidth, evidenced by strong stress-ng multi-core metrics and 3,782.81 GB/sec cached small-block read speeds. Application-level evaluations reflect strong results for network-bound and parallel execution paths, reaching 72.72 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads, 44.93 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and high Clang software compilation throughput.

A noticeable tradeoff in the Neoverse-N1 architecture is single-threaded performance. Single-core Geekbench and compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 test in lower benchmark tiers. Furthermore, CPU-based large language model inference demonstrates weak throughput, particularly during text generation phases, showing that mathematical acceleration without vector extensions like AVX or discrete GPUs is constrained. From an operational efficiency perspective, the high core density and standard compute-optimized memory allocation provide high concurrent transaction capability per core for ARM64-compatible architectures.

Given its 100 Gbps network pipe and strong multi-core scaling, Amazon Web Services c6gn.16xlarge is suited for network-intensive workloads, distributed in-memory caching nodes, high-traffic web serving clusters, large-scale software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices compiled for arm64.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.16xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized instance powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It includes 128.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) and baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, operating on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance features no local storage or GPUs, relying on networked block volumes. In performance benchmarks, the platform demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing, software compilation throughput, Redis operations, and static web serving speeds, enabled by its high core count and network interface. Single-threaded metrics and CPU-based LLM inference are comparatively weak due to per-core execution limitations and the absence of specialized x86 vector extensions. It is primarily suited for high-throughput networking services, distributed caching, parallel build farms, and multi-threaded container workloads.
